clue.text: Is he employed in the removal business?

definitions.text: Is he employed in the removal business?

parts.words: Is he employed in the removal business?
parts.note: a removal man's job is to move things about, so someone in that line works at moving loads; really it means a person whose working hours rotate

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone works for a furniture removal firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends to be about a removals firm; the real sense is a person who works in rotating periods, day or night.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone in a 'shifting' line of work, punning on the rota of turns a factory worker covers.

clue.text: Not killing one in season

indicators.note: the word one goes inside the season, so in signals a container

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A hunter decides not to shoot anything during a particular time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting a creature live, showing mercy rather than slaying it, is a synonym sense.

clue.text: Long story mostly rejected by the dailies

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
mostly means not all of the word dailies is used; its final two letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A long feature article is spiked by the daily newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DAILIES to DAILI, and 'rejected' turns that round. 'the' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is a very lengthy narrative poem.

clue.text: Sketch to be cut?

definitions.meaning: a quick small drawing or brief outline is a ... sketch
the horny plate on a thumb is something that gets trimmed with clippers

explanation.surface: An editor wonders whether a comic sketch should be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief rough summary is a thumbnail sketch; and a digit's nail is what one clips short.

clue.text: Port gets round prohibition

parts.note: O is round in shape
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A harbour town finds a way to get around an embargo.
explanation.walkthrough: OBAN is a fishing and ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a harbour town in Argyll, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Observe inner need when profoundly involved

indicators.note: inner tells us the word need sits within the synonym for observe

parts.note: to observe a rule or festival is to keep it

explanation.surface: Advice to notice your deep-seated needs when you are deeply engaged in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observe' looks like 'watch' but means keep, as in keeping the Sabbath; NEED goes inside it after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deeply embroiled in something is being up to one's knees in it, an idiom.

clue.text: Poet of Irish extraction

indicators.note: extraction suggests the letters are pulled out and set down in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet whose ancestry is Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Irish extraction' reads as ancestry, but 'extraction' rearranges IRISH; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu sage or inspired seer, the composer of Vedic hymns, hence a poet.

clue.text: Can be seen nearing disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A catastrophe approaching is already visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within sight or reach of the eye is visible, so the phrase means it is observable.

clue.text: He might put things in better focus for you

definitions.text: He might put things in better focus for you

parts.words: He might put things in better focus for you
parts.note: reads like a helpful counsellor clarifying your problems, but literally describes the person who prescribes lenses to sharpen your sight

explanation.surface: A friend or adviser who helps you see matters more clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the professional who tests eyes and supplies spectacles.

clue.text: Sour drug aristocratic pupil consumed

parts.note: acid is slang for the drug LSD
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A posh student takes a hallucinogen and turns sour.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something sharp or tart in taste is to make it acid, a verb sense.

clue.text: Quietly leaving meal that is very good

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so one letter is taken out of the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
P is piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Slipping away from dinner without a fuss is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent, first-rate: an informal synonym for outstanding.

clue.text: Ibadan members at tribal conference

indicators.note: the members, the letters of the city name, are rearranged into a new grouping

explanation.surface: Delegates from the Nigerian city of Ibadan attend a meeting of tribes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibadan is a large city in Nigeria; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a southern African gathering of elders or chiefs to discuss matters, a council meeting.

clue.text: Extra item not about dependency on drugs

indicators.note: not about means the letter for about is left out

parts.note: addiction is dependency on drugs
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A further thing that is not related to drug dependence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added on, a supplement, is an extra thing.

clue.text: Cheerful despite being blown about in gale

indicators.note: tossed around by the wind, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone stays good-humoured while battered by a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-humoured: a synonym for jolly.

clue.text: One very close to you

parts.note: sounds like a dear friend or relative, but means the person living in the adjacent house

explanation.surface: A loved one, someone dear to your heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the resident of the adjoining house is physically nearest.

clue.text: The interval is not a generous period

parts.note: mean means stingy, not generous
a period is a time

explanation.surface: A complaint that a break was ungenerously short.
explanation.definitionFit: The intervening period, between two events, is a phrase for the meanwhile.

clue.text: See 14
Be arrogant about the animal (beaver or otherwise)

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Behaving haughtily towards a beaver or some other creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about the animal' also gives OVER + BEAR, a second route; the bracket supplies an anagram of BEAVER OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer or behave haughtily is to act in a high-handed, overweening way.

clue.text: Plant used by animal taking cover

parts.note: a fox is an animal
a glove is a cover for the hand

explanation.surface: A creature takes shelter under a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis, a tall flowering plant with bell-shaped blooms, is an example of a plant.

clue.text: He starts to sink

definitions.meaning: a person who establishes or starts an organisation
of a ship, to fill with water and go down

explanation.surface: A man begins to go under.
explanation.definitionFit: One who starts an institution is its originator; and a ship that sinks is said to go to the bottom.

clue.text: Remarkable way to transmit a message

definitions.meaning: notable or striking, as in an outstanding achievement
a sign, light or flag used to convey information

explanation.surface: An impressive new means of communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable achievement is a signal one; and a gesture or flare conveying information is another sense.

clue.text: Cavalrymen dance

definitions.meaning: a nineteenth-century quadrille danced by sets of couples

explanation.surface: Horse soldiers take to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers armed with lances; and the Lancers was a square dance for four couples.

clue.text: It is not above a sailor to bowl thus

parts.note: under is the opposite of above
RM stands for Royal Marine, a seagoing serviceman

explanation.surface: A seaman is not too proud to bowl in this style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' introduces the wordplay. In cricket, bowling with the arm below shoulder height is frowned on; 'not above' suggests pride but means under.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering a ball with the hand below shoulder level is the style named, so it describes the bowling action.

clue.text: Cold man getting in the drink

indicators.note: getting in tells us the word for man enters the drink

parts.note: rum is a drink
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man ends up in the alcohol, or falls into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' suggests the sea, but means RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery discharge from the nose and eyes, as with a chill, so it means a catarrhal cold.

clue.text: Feature about work he composed

indicators.note: about means around, so the feature surrounds the work

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
OP is opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An article about a piece he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish composer of nocturnes and mazurkas is identified by his writing music.

clue.text: Greek god of the underworld pipeline

definitions.meaning: the ruler of the dead, also called Hades
the wartime Pipe Line Under The Ocean, laid under the Channel in 1944

explanation.surface: A deity of the dead linked with a pipeline.
explanation.definitionFit: The lord of the dead in classical myth; and the 1944 fuel conduit beneath the English Channel bore the same acronym.

clue.text: Might he get off free?

parts.note: reads as asking whether a suspect escapes punishment, alluding to the phrase for going unpunished, and asks which nationality's man that would be

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a defendant will escape punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone from Scotland, punning on the idiom for escaping without penalty.

clue.text: Controlled the cattle?

definitions.meaning: a herd of animals being driven to market

explanation.surface: Someone managed the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Steered a car is a past-tense sense; and a herd of beasts moving together is another.

clue.text: Pen put in an envelope

definitions.meaning: a document or item sent along with a letter

explanation.surface: A pen slipped inside a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fenced paddock for animals is one sense; and something sent with a letter is another.

clue.text: Deserving an order, otherwise promises to pay

parts.note: the Order of Merit is a British honour
or means otherwise
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Someone worthy of a decoration, or else owing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthy of praise or reward is a synonym for praiseworthy.
